correctness.rationale: PASS: The folded cube is a quotient Cayley graph F2^(n+1)/<all-ones> with generating set the n+1 coordinate cosets; translations and all generator permutations prove edge transitivity, including formerly distinguished antipodal edges. Even Walsh character subsets index Laplacian eigenvalues 2|S|, so an edge source-sink solution is expressible as finite character sum. Reciprocal integral yields U_j=∫_(1/2)^1[z^(n−j)(1−z)^j−z^j(1−z)^(n−j)]dz, strictly decreasing in j and antisymmetric U_(n−j)=−U_j. Thus all cube-edge drops sum exactly n/2, antipodal drops sum B_(2k−1)=B_(2k)=1−4^(−k)binom(2k,k) by binomial-majority integration by parts. These are full cut-column absolute sums. Effective resistance diagonal is (2^n−1)/[(n+1)2^(n−1)]=2(1−2^(−n))/(n+1) by rank(Q)=2^n−1 and edge transitivity; |I−Q| column sum equals |Q| column sum +1−2q. Independently built full graph incidence/Laplacian and pseudoinverse for n=3,4,5,6, checking all edge columns and both closed forms, plus read exact rational package checker. The proof establishes every integer n≥5; tests are finite corroboration.

value.rationale: PASS: This solves the exact natural endpoint projection norms of a canonical graph family obtained by adding the antipodal matching, not a recomputation for the original cube. Edge-transitivity and a binomial-majority law produce a new central-binomial correction with odd/even pairing and precise excess over ordinary-cube norm, useful for graph cycle-space and transportation-cost projection estimates.

final_claim: For n≥5, the canonical orthogonal cut and complementary cycle projections on the antipodally augmented binary n-cube F_n have l1→l1 and l∞→l∞ norms respectively n/2+1−c_k and n/2+2−c_k−4(1−2^(−n))/(n+1), where k=ceil(n/2), c_k=4^(−k)*binom(2k,k). Each edge column attains the norm; the cut norm exceeds the ordinary cube by 1/2−c_k.
limitations: Simple unweighted real graph, n≥5, canonical orthogonal cut/cycle projection only.
